# Configuration

Every setting lives in `config/config.json` with its default value. A deployment overrides what it needs in `config.local/config.json`, which is deep-merged over `config/config.json` at startup and on every file change. Plain objects merge key by key, and arrays and scalars in the local file replace the base value whole. `src/config/files.ts` says which file the loader reads, and `src/config.ts` and `src/hot.ts` read it.

Both files reload without a restart. Code reads `hot.config` at the moment of use, so an edit takes effect on the next request. A file that fails to parse (half-written JSON, an editor temp file) is ignored: the previous good value stays live and the error is logged. At startup, invalid JSON still throws so a broken deployment fails fast.

Any string value in the merged config may hold `${env:NAME}` (`NAME` is letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit). After the merge, each reference is replaced with the variable's value from `.env`, so a credential can stay in `.env` while the config holds only the reference. An unset variable becomes an empty string and is logged once (`config: env ref unset`). `/config set` keeps the reference in `config.local/config.json`, and every reload resolves it again.

The tables of this document are generated by `scripts/config-doc.ts` from the settings schema, `src/config/schema.ts`, which holds every key with its types, its default, one line of text and the module that reads it. Its entries live in `src/config/schema/<section>.ts`. A new key gets an entry there and in `config/config.json`, then `node scripts/config-doc.ts > docs/configuration.md` writes this file again. `tests/config-schema.test.ts` holds the defaults equal to `config/config.json`, `tests/config-check.test.ts` checks that each reader module names its key, and `tests/config-doc.test.ts` fails while this file differs from the generator's output.

`/config check` in the owner's chat and `neptunia doctor` check `config.local/config.json` against the schema and name each key the schema does not know and each key whose value has a type the key does not take (`src/config/check.ts`). The core starts on such a file all the same.

## Where the private files live

By default everything sits in the checkout: `config/` and `prompts/` (tracked), your `.env`, `config.local/` and `prompts.local/`, and the `data/` directory the bot writes to. `config/` holds `config.json` (the settings), `labels.json` (the wording code inserts, see [Prompt contract](prompt-contract.md#labels)) and `tools.json` (the tool texts), and `config.local/` holds the same three files for a deployment, each deep-merged over its tracked file, plus `interfaces/<name>.json`, which `neptunia interface run <name>` lays over the interface package's own `config.json`. Two environment variables move the private parts out of the checkout:

| Variable | Default | What lives there |
|---|---|---|
| `NEPTUNIA_PRIVATE_DIR` | the checkout | `.env`, `keys.json` (the model keys, see [Keys](keys.md)), `config.local/`, `prompts.local/`, `clients.json`, `clients/`, `cli/` (the chat's picture and history, see [The neptunia command](cli.md)) |
| `NEPTUNIA_DATA_DIR` | `data/` in the checkout | everything the bot writes: `guilds/`, `state.json`, `usage.json`, `metrics.json`, caches |

Set them in the process environment (for example `Environment=` in the systemd unit), not in `.env`: the bot reads `.env` from the private directory, so it needs to know that directory first. A relative path is resolved against the checkout. An edit to a file in `config.local/` or `prompts.local/` inside the private directory still reloads live. The tools read the same two variables; `--data` overrides the data path. At start the bot logs the three resolved directories (`index: paths`). `deploy/neptunia-bot.service` shows the recommended layout.

## The old layout of the private files

A private directory laid out the old way keeps its settings in `config.local.json` and its labels in a flat `prompts.local/labels.json`, with no `model` and `owner` sections. The engine reads both as it reads the new files and logs one warning per start that names `scripts/config-files-move.ts`. A directory with a file at both its old and its new place refuses the start with a message that names the same tool.

`node scripts/config-files-move.ts --private <dir>` says what it would move, and `--apply` moves it. `config.local.json` goes to `config.local/config.json` byte for byte. `prompts.local/labels.json` goes to `config.local/labels.json`, split by the checkout's `config/labels.json`: a key the tracked file holds under `owner` goes to `owner`, every other key to `model`. When a file sits at both places with the same content (the labels compared after the split), the run deletes the old copy. With different content it refuses, names the old file and changes nothing. A second run finds nothing to do.

## Clients and their tokens

`clients.json` in the private directory names every client that may connect to the core's socket, and `clients/<name>.token` holds each client's token. An entry has the client's `kind` (`interface`, `cli` or `agent`), the `iface` an interface's events must carry, the `tokenFile` relative to the private directory, and `permissions`. The core reads both files at every envelope (`src/interface/principals.ts`), so a change applies at once and a rotated or revoked token closes that client's link. Without `clients.json` the core makes one token at start for the interface it runs in its own process, and nothing else connects. A `clients.json` that is not valid JSON lets no client in. See [Interfaces](interfaces.md#clients-and-principals).

An entry may also carry `boardRoles`, the client's roles on the task board: any of `owner`, `reviewer`, `worker`, `scheduler`, `persona`, `watcher` and `errand-runner`. The board reads them at every call (`src/board/board.ts`). An entry without `boardRoles`, a name outside that list and a client absent from the file get no right on the board. See [The core](core.md#the-task-board).

The owner's `neptunia` chat is the client `cli` of kind `cli`, which runs every command with the owner's rights. An interface client sends no command: the link refuses its `command.requested` whatever its `permissions` hold. A client of kind `agent` is a development agent of the task board: it says hello under `agent`, sends only the board's `task.*` commands (`neptunia task`, see [The neptunia command](cli.md)), and the board lets it do what its `boardRoles` allow. A `task.*` command of the `cli` client goes to the board too, under the client's own `boardRoles`. The board's builtin principal `persona`, which her board tools call as, holds the role `persona` alone, and an entry named `persona` adds nothing to it.

`scripts/client-token.ts` writes both files, at mode `0600`, in the private directory `NEPTUNIA_PRIVATE_DIR` names. It never prints a token.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/client-token.ts add <name> --kind <kind> [--iface <iface>] [--permission <p>] [--roles <role>,<role>]` | Makes a token and the client's entry. `--kind interface` needs `--iface`. `--permission` may repeat. `--roles` writes the comma list as `boardRoles`, with any kind, and a role outside the board's list writes nothing |
| `node scripts/client-token.ts rotate <name>` | Writes a new token over the old one |
| `node scripts/client-token.ts revoke <name>` | Removes the entry and the token file |

The token file belongs to the user the client runs as: `chown` it after `add` and after `rotate`.

## Keys that moved

The persona's skills are tools in the settings. `src/config-moves.ts` holds the old names as an ordered list, and `src/config.ts` applies it to the private settings file before the file is laid over `config/config.json`, so an old key still sets the value of its new name. Each load that moves a key logs one warning with the counts. Where both names are set, the new one wins.

| Old key | New key |
|---|---|
| `skills.*` | `tools.*` |
| `bot.access."skills.describe"` | `bot.access."tools.describe"` |
| `bot.access."task.run"`, `"task.status"`, `"task.read"`, `"task.resolve"`, `"task.cancel"`, `"task.list"` | `bot.access."errand.run"`, `"errand.status"`, `"errand.read"`, `"errand.resolve"`, `"errand.cancel"`, `"errand.list"` |
| `bot.access."intent.set"`, `"intent.update"`, `"intent.cancel"`, `"intent.list"` | `bot.access."intention.set"`, `"intention.update"`, `"intention.cancel"`, `"intention.list"` |
| `agents.opencodePath`, `toolResultChars`, `keepFilesHours`, `recentLines`, `maxOpen`, `resultMaxChars`, `unreadShown`, `resultRetrySeconds`, `resultCooldownSeconds` | the same names under `errands.*` |
| `agents.<name>.search.provider` | `agents.<name>.searchProvider` |
| `llm.helperTimeoutMs` | `llm.analyzerTimeoutMs` |
| `innerLife.heartbeat.*` | the same names under `heartbeat.*` |
| `diary.*` | the same names under `selfreflection.*` |
| `selfdev.*` | the same names under `selfimprovement.*` |
| `innerLife.wakes.selfimprovement.*` | the same names under `selfimprovement.*` |
| `innerLife.wakes.heartbeat.*` | the same names under `heartbeat.*` |
| `innerLife.wakes.<kind>.*` of the other wake kinds | `wakes.kinds.<kind>.*` |
| every other key of `innerLife.*` | the same name under `wakes.*` |
| `features.innerLife` | `features.wakes` |

Seven keys have no reader any more and are dropped: the grants `bot.access."memory.refresh.channel"`, `"memory.refresh.server"` and `"memory.refresh.user"`, `agents.maxDownloadBytes`, `agents.thinker.contextLimit` and `contextHard`, and `agents.ledger.socket`. A section a dropped key leaves empty goes with it. The load log line counts them as `dropped` beside `moved` and `shadowed`.

`node scripts/config-migrate.ts --dry-run` prints each move for the private settings file (or `--file <path>`), each dropped key as `<path> dropped (no reader)`, and `--apply` writes the result into the file. A second run finds nothing to move. `--dry-run --compare-with <config.json>` reads the settings the moves touch twice, once the old way over the given `config.json` and once through the current readers over this checkout's, and prints `equal: <n>, differ: <n>` with one line per difference. It exits 1 on any difference. `--self <id>` names the persona's user id when `bot.self` is not set, so the grants can be compared.

The owner commands that edit the private settings file (`set`, `access grant`, `access revoke`) apply the same moves to the file before they read it, so a write never leaves a key of an old name beside the new one.

The tool texts moved too: `prompts/skills.json` is `config/tools.json`, and a deployment's `prompts.local/skills.json` is `config.local/tools.json` with the entry `skills.describe` renamed `tools.describe`. The `skills` section of `prompts.local/labels.json` is the section `tools`. The errand and intention names changed in the same layer: the ten tool entries `task.*` and `intent.*` of the tool texts are `errand.*` and `intention.*`, and in `labels.json` the section `tasks` is `errands`, the trigger `task` is `errand`, the note `task-missing` is `errand-missing`, the reason codes `no-task`, `task-ended` and `wait-without-task` are `no-errand`, `errand-ended` and `wait-without-errand`, and the placeholder `{task}` is `{errand}` in the texts that carry it. `node scripts/tools-file-move.ts --dry-run` and `--apply` do all of it, read `--dir` or `NEPTUNIA_PRIVATE_DIR`, and change no file when any part is refused. The engine refuses to start while `prompts.local/skills.json` exists.

## Rails

Two hard rails that must stay on:

- **50 000 tokens per request** (`llm.maxRequestTokens`). Every request the bot sends is budgeted against this cap. The prompt builder trims sections by priority to fit.
- **Daily request cap** (`llm.maxRequestsPerDay`, default 5000). Every model request counts (requests on every model role, probes, tools, hedged duplicates). It is the one daily count the engine refuses at.

## The config cut

The settings hold the keys someone would change, the timeouts, budgets, retention and recovery limits, the privacy switches and the two rails. `src/config/cut.ts` lists every key the cut of 2026-10-31 took out and what it became: a named constant in the module that reads it, with the value production ran with; code that always runs, for a switch that was on (the `features.*` switches and the rollouts of `memoryDb`); nothing, for a switch that was off and the code it reached (`features.dryRun`, `features.spontaneous`, `features.eavesdrop`, `features.turnPlanner`, `pace.typingWhilePreparing`, `bot.dryRunChannelId`, `spontaneous.*`); and nothing, for a daily cap, whose counter went with it. `features.privateMessages` and `features.privateLikeServer` are `private.enabled` and `private.likeServer`, and the per-wake budgets are one `wakes.kinds.*.<field>` entry each.

`src/config.ts` takes the cut keys out of the private settings file at each load, after the moves, and logs one warning line with the counts. `node scripts/config-migrate.ts --dry-run` prints `<key> dropped (<becomes>)` for each, `<key> differs: live <json>, constant <json>` for a live value apart from the constant that replaced it, `<from> -> <to>` for the two privacy switches, and `<key> -> config.local/interfaces/discord.json` for a key of the Discord package. `--apply` writes the file and merges the Discord keys under what `config.local/interfaces/discord.json` already holds.

`node scripts/config-effective.ts --snapshot <file> --private <dir>` writes the effective settings of a private layer and the objects the readers derive from them, and `--compare <file> --private <dir>` prints each leaf that differs as `<config|settings>.<path>: before <json>, after <json>`, marked ` (declared)` when the cut declares it, then `equal: <n>, differ: <n>, declared: <n>`. It exits 1 on an undeclared difference.

## The Discord package's settings

`discord.intents.presences` and `discord.intents.members` (default `false`, the privileged intents), `context.maxUrlChars` (default `200`, the longest a URL in a message's text reads) and `media.embedTextChars` (default `200`, the characters of an embed's title and of its text) live in `interfaces/discord/config.json`. The interface reads them over the core's settings with `config.local/interfaces/discord.json` over both (`src/config/files.ts#readInterfaceConfig`), in the core's process and as a unit alike. The voice-state intent (voice channels in `<people_now>`) is not privileged and always requested.

| `interfaces.mode` | string | `"inprocess"` | Where the interfaces run. `inprocess` starts the Discord interface inside the core's process. `units` starts the core with no interface, and each interface runs in its own unit (`neptunia interface run <name>`). Read once at the start of `src/index.ts`, and any other value stops the start | `src/core.ts` |
| `interfaces.drainMs` | number | `10000` | How long a disable (`/interface disable`) gives the actions in flight to an interface (milliseconds) before the core ends them `unknown` | `src/core.ts` |

## `models`

Three groups, the same three the status card shows (`/status full`). Each role is set independently with its own default, so changing one never moves another.

- **`models.base`**: the bot's own requests. The core decides and speaks as the persona; each other model role gathers, describes, extracts or finds.
- **`models.errands`**: delegated agents. Each runs its own OpenCode loop as a separate process. See [Errands](errands.md).
- **`models.development`**: agents that work on the repository, not on the persona's behalf. The engine only describes them and shows their spend.

### `models.base`

`core`, `memory`, `analyzer` and `embedding` are mandatory and refuse a `null`. `vision`, `video`, `drawing` and `speech` ship as `null`, which turns the role off; a model id turns it on. See [Media](media.md#optional-roles-that-are-off).

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `models.base.core` | string, boolean | `"anthropic/claude-opus-4.6"` | The persona's model. Purposes: `reply`, `memory-voice` | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |
| `models.base.memory` | string, boolean | `"anthropic/claude-opus-4.6"` | Her memory session and description review model. Same default as `core`, not a copy. Its key is `llm.keyByRole.memory` and never falls back | `src/llm/roles.ts` |
| `models.base.analyzer` | string, boolean | `"openai/gpt-6.1-sol"` | Picks options (address, room, route, split, gif-pick, missed, etc.), plans searches and turns sources into notes. Pin one purpose to another model with `byPurpose` | `src/behavior/mention.ts` |
| `models.base.vision` | string, boolean, null | `null` | Describes pictures (describe, relook, avatar). Off while null | `src/behavior/mention.ts` |
| `models.base.video` | string, boolean, null | `null` | Watches video and GIFs, looks again on questions. Off while null | `src/behavior/mention.ts` |
| `models.base.embedding` | string, boolean | `"openai/text-embedding-3-large"` | Turns text into vectors for meaning search. `embed.dimensions` sets the width | `src/llm/embed.ts` |
| `models.base.speech` | string, boolean, null | `null` | Speaks her text aloud through the speech endpoint. Named on the status card, never probed. Off while null | `src/speech/synth.ts` |
| `models.base.drawing` | string, boolean, null | `null` | Generates pictures through the Images API. Only `openai/*` and `google/*` families. Off while null | `src/llm/images.ts` |

A role set to `false` has no model. Its tool calls (`media.look` for `vision` and `video`, `draw.create` for `drawing`, `voice.say` for `speech`) go to the core model when the core declares the role's ability in `models.abilities`, and answer `ability-unavailable` otherwise. `/status` lists the role as failing and `neptunia doctor` warns about it. `null` or a missing key is the role's default model. The same route applies while a role is failing globally (see [Media](media.md#when-a-model-role-is-down)).

### `models.abilities` and `models.byPurpose`

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `models.abilities` | map | `{ "anthropic/claude-opus-4.6": ["text", "imagesIn"], "google/gemini-3.8-flash": ["text", "imagesIn", "videoIn"], "openai/text-embedding-3-large": ["embeddings"], "elevenlabs/eleven-v4": ["audioOut"], "openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare": ["imagesOut"] }` | What each model can do, keyed by model id: a list of `text`, `imagesIn`, `imagesOut`, `videoIn`, `audioOut` and `embeddings`. A model without an entry has `text` only | `src/llm/roles.ts` |

Only the core model's list in `models.abilities` is read, by `src/tools/gateway.ts#abilityRoute`, when a tool role is down. A core model without an entry has `text` only, so a down tool role answers `ability-unavailable`. A deployment whose core reads pictures gives its core model the list `["text", "imagesIn"]`.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `models.byPurpose` | map | `{}` | Model ids keyed by purpose string (`reply`, `lookup`, `recall-summary`, `diary-plan`, `planner`, `web-search` and the like). A match on purpose wins over the role's model. Not probed by the status card | `src/llm/embed.ts` |

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |

| `llm.probeTimeoutMs` | number | `30000` | Timeout of each model probe and of the key reads of the status card (ms) | `src/tools/impl/status.ts` |
| `llm.analyzerTimeoutMs` | number | `30000` | Timeout of a request on a model role other than the core's, made alongside the turn (route classifier, search classifier, recall summary). Past this the request is abandoned | `src/llm/embed.ts` |
| `llm.retries` | number | `2` | Retries on transient HTTP errors (408/429/5xx) and network failures. A daily-quota 429 is thrown at once | `src/llm/embed.ts` |
| `llm.maxRequestsPerDay` | number | `5000` | Daily request cap | `src/behavior/pull-fetch.ts` |
| `llm.provider` | map, null | `null` | OpenRouter `provider` routing object, passed verbatim | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |
| `llm.providerByModel` | map | `{}` | Per-model provider routing. See the resolution order below | `src/llm/embed.ts` |
| `llm.reasoningByRole` | map | `{}` | The reasoning effort of a role by role name, `{ "effort": "low" }`, `medium` or `high`, sent as `reasoning` on each request of the role that has no reasoning of its own. Read for `memory`, `analyzer`, `vision` and `video`, never for the core. `/model set <role> <model> --effort <level>` writes it | `src/llm/roles.ts` |
| `llm.keyByRole` | map | `{ "scout": "OPENROUTER_ERRAND_KEY", "server": "OPENROUTER_ERRAND_KEY", "drawing": "OPENROUTER_ERRAND_KEY", "thinker": "OPENROUTER_DEV_KEY", "dev": "OPENROUTER_DEV_KEY", "memory": "OPENROUTER_MEMORY_KEY" }` | Read only while the private layer has no `keys.json`; with one, the key store decides (see [Keys](keys.md)). Maps a role name to the NAME of a `.env` variable holding an OpenRouter key, or to a list of names. The first name of a list is the primary key. When a request gets HTTP 402, or 429 with a body naming credits or balance, the role moves to the next name and the request is repeated once on it; after the last name it goes back to the first. When every key failed within a minute the request fails with `keys-exhausted` and the role counts as down until 00:00 UTC. Read at every request. A role not in the map falls back to `OPENROUTER_CORE_KEY`; the `core` role then uses `OPENROUTER_CORE_BACKUP_KEY` as its second key when that variable is set. A name that is not an `OPENROUTER_` variable or is unset is left out. The `memory` role is the exception: with `OPENROUTER_MEMORY_KEY` unset, the session is not configured and no request goes out on any other key | `src/core.ts` |
| `llm.keys` | map | `{}` | Read only while the private layer has no `keys.json`; with one, each core key carries its own grant (see [Keys](keys.md)). The grant of each key, by the NAME of its `.env` variable: `{ "grant": USD, "resetDay": 1 to 31 }`. The balance of a key is its grant minus the cost of the requests that went out on it since the last reset (00:00 UTC on `resetDay`, the last day of a shorter month), summed from `data/usage.json`; no call to the provider. The balances of the core keys set the turns line of her wake view. A key without an entry counts 0 and is named on the status card as unconfigured | `src/core.ts` |
| `llm.cache.ttl` | string | `"1h"` | Cache TTL for the markers on the system message and the stable user prefix: `"1h"` or `"5m"` | `src/behavior/prompt.ts` |
| `llm.cache.roles` | array | `["core"]` | Model roles whose requests get the cache marker. Add `analyzer` to cache its requests too | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |
| `llm.cache.models` | array | `["anthropic/"]` | Model id prefixes whose provider accepts the `cache_control` marker | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |
| `llm.hedge.roles` | array | `["analyzer"]` | Roles whose calls are hedged (two concurrent attempts, first to finish wins) | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |
| `llm.hedge.afterMs` | number | `2500` | Milliseconds before the second attempt starts. `0` or below turns hedging off | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |
| `llm.hedge.timeoutMs` | number | `8000` | Milliseconds from the first attempt's start at which both are aborted if neither returned | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |
| `llm.hedge.longTimeoutMs` | number | `20000` | Timeout used when the caller marks the request `long: true` (the route classifier does this for a large channel list) | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |

### Provider routing resolution

For one request the provider is resolved in order: a per-call pin, then the longest matching `providerByModel` key for the request's role (`<prefix>@<role>`), then the longest matching role-less key (`<prefix>`), then `llm.provider`, then nothing. A role-specific key always beats a role-less key for the same model. A route may carry `"byok": true` (never sent to OpenRouter): an answer OpenRouter served from its own capacity instead of your provider account fails without a retry.

## `memoryDb`

The memory database. One SQLite file, kept in sync with the stored memory. See [Memory](memory.md).

### `memoryDb.session`

Her memory session: she reads new chat lines of one scope and says what she keeps, in her own voice, on the model `models.base.memory` and the key `llm.keyByRole.memory`. See [Memory](memory.md).

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `memoryDb.session.mode` | string | `"off"` | `off`: nothing runs. `shadow`: proposed changes are recorded as decisions, nothing applied. `apply`: changes are written to the database | `src/memory/db/describe.ts` |
| `memoryDb.session.maxMessages` | number | `200` | Lines in one request | `src/memory/db/session.ts` |
| `memoryDb.session.minMessages` | number | `5` | A scope with fewer new lines waits | `src/memory/db/session.ts` |
| `memoryDb.session.minLines` | number | `0` | A settled session of this many lines or fewer waits and joins the next batch of its scope. `0` writes every session at once | `src/memory/db/session.ts` |
| `memoryDb.session.batchLines` | number | `30` | Joined lines at which a scope with waiting sessions is written | `src/memory/db/session.ts` |
| `memoryDb.session.maxWaitHours` | number | `24` | Age of the oldest waiting line at which its scope is written, whatever the size | `src/memory/db/session.ts` |
| `memoryDb.session.sweepsPerScopePerDay` | number | `24` | Sweeps that reach one scope per UTC day | `src/memory/db/session.ts` |
| `memoryDb.session.everyMinutes` | number | `60` | Minutes between sweeps (with `mode` `apply`) | `src/memory/db/session.ts` |
| `memoryDb.session.reviewsPerDay` | number | `6` | Description reviews per UTC day. `0` disables | `src/memory/db/service.ts` |
| `memoryDb.session.since` | string, null | `null` | An ISO date; a scope with no cursor starts from this date. `null`: the first line | `src/memory/db/session.ts` |
| `memoryDb.session.maxPeople` | number | `12` | People shown per request, most active first | `src/memory/db/session.ts` |
| `memoryDb.session.claimsPerPerson` | number | `30` | Claims listed per person | `src/memory/db/session.ts` |
| `memoryDb.session.selfMax` | number | `40` | Her own claims listed | `src/memory/db/session.ts` |
| `memoryDb.session.episodesMax` | number | `20` | Episodes listed | `src/memory/db/session.ts` |

## `pace`

How long each stage of a turn may take. A request on a model role other than `core` that misses its deadline is dropped. A turn whose answer is not in hand by `dropAfterMs` is dropped entirely.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pace.prepareMs` | number | `6000` | Milliseconds from the turn's start before the voice request. Everything before the LLM call must finish here. `0` removes the limit | `src/turn/phases/request/stages.ts` |
| `pace.prepareSearchMs` | number | `18000` | Extended deadline while the search classifier runs. `0` removes the limit | `src/turn/settings.ts` |
| `pace.prepareMediaMs` | number | `20000` | Extended deadline on a direct call whose trigger carries a picture, GIF or video. `0` removes it | `src/turn/settings.ts` |
| `pace.dropAfterMs` | number | `120000` | If the finished answer has not arrived by this time, the turn is dropped. `0` removes it | `src/turn/phases/request/setup.ts` |
| `pace.replyHedgeMs` | number | `30000` | On a direct call, when the reply has no answer after this long, a second request is sent. `0` = one attempt only | `src/llm/openrouter.ts` |
| `pace.settleMs` | number | `3000` | Wait for the person to stop writing before reading the chat, so quick messages are answered whole | `src/behavior/pipeline.ts` |
| `pace.settleMaxMs` | number | `8000` | The longest that wait may run from the calling message | `src/turn/sends.ts` |

| `selfimprovement.inputTokens` | number, null | `null` | The input token budget of a selfimprovement wake; null: the loop budget | `src/tools/access.ts` |

## `selfreflection`

Settings for the diary, which this mechanic writes. `enabled` switches the scheduled posts. See [Diary](diary.md).

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `selfreflection.enabled` | boolean | `true` | Whether her diary posts on its day plan. Off, the scheduler plans and posts nothing; a forced post still runs | `src/behavior/diary.ts` |
| `selfreflection.channelId` | string | `""` | The seed of the diary's first mirror: schema v15 makes this channel's place a `diary` mirror, and `scripts/config-migrate.ts --apply --db <memory.db>` then takes the key out of the local file. Nothing else reads it | `src/memory/db/service.ts` |
| `selfreflection.world` | boolean | `false` | Include `prompts/world.md` as a `<world>` block in diary requests | `src/behavior/prompt.ts` |
| `selfreflection.windows` | array | `[{ "from": 7, "to": 11, "posts": [0, 0] }, { "from": 12, "to": 16, "posts": [0, 1] }, { "from": 18, "to": 1, "posts": [0, 2] }, { "from": 1, "to": 5, "posts": [0, 1] }]` | Posting windows in `bot.timezone`. Each has `from`, `to` (hours) and `posts: [min, max]` | `src/behavior/diary.ts` |
| `selfreflection.quietDayChance` | number | `0.3` | Chance of no posts for the whole day | `src/behavior/diary.ts` |
| `selfreflection.forceWaitMs` | number | `120000` | Milliseconds a forced post waits for a running turn | `src/behavior/diary.ts` |
| `selfreflection.loop.maxSteps` | number | `2` | Further requests one diary post makes | `src/turn/settings.ts` |
| `selfreflection.loop.timeBudgetMs` | number | `600000` | How long calls and follow-ups may run | `src/turn/settings.ts` |
| `selfreflection.planMaxOutputTokens` | number | `2000` | Max output tokens for the plan request | `src/turn/diary.ts` |
| `selfreflection.planTimeoutMs` | number | `60000` | Timeout for the plan request (ms) | `src/turn/diary.ts` |

Default windows:

```json
[
  { "from": 7,  "to": 11, "posts": [0, 0] },
  { "from": 12, "to": 16, "posts": [0, 1] },
  { "from": 18, "to": 1,  "posts": [0, 2] },
  { "from": 1,  "to": 5,  "posts": [0, 1] }
]
```

## `agents`

The settings of one agent live in its profile, `agents/<name>/profile.json` (see [the agents folder](../agents/README.md)). A deployment overrides a setting under `agents.<name>` of `config.local/config.json`, and `agentSettings(name, config)` in `src/agent-runner/profiles.ts` lays the override over the profile, a nested object merged key by key. The core, the agent runner and the dispatcher all read an agent's settings through it.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agents` | map | `{}` | Per agent name, overrides of the settings in `agents/<name>/profile.json`, laid over the profile key by key | `src/agent-runner/profiles.ts` |

The keys of a profile and the values the shipped profiles carry:

| Profile key | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `false` for `scout` and `server` | Runs the worker. Workers only |
| `cost` | `scout` and `server` `{ "input": 2, "output": 6 }`, `thinker` `{ "input": 4, "output": 20 }`, `dev` `{ "input": 2, "output": 10 }` | Model price (USD per million tokens) for OpenCode's estimate and the spend figures |
| `socket` | `"/run/neptunia-agent-scout/sock"`, `"/run/neptunia-agent-server/sock"` | Unix socket of the runner. Workers only |
| `out` | `"/var/lib/neptunia-agent-scout/out"`, `"/var/lib/neptunia-agent-server/out"` | Directory for output files. Workers only |
| `limits` | `scout` `{ "steps": 25, "seconds": 300 }`, `server` `{ "steps": 20, "seconds": 120 }`, `thinker` `{ "steps": 400, "minutes": 60 }`, `dev` `{ "steps": 300, "minutes": 60 }` | Caps of one run |
| `daily` | `{ "tasks": 40 }` for `scout` and `server` | Tasks per day. Workers only |
| `searchProvider` | `"exa"` for `scout`, `null` for `server` | Web search provider, `exa` or `parallel`. Workers only |

The thinker and the dev agent run outside the engine; the bot only shows their spend on the status card.

## `board`

The task board's settings (`src/board/board.ts#boardSettings` and `#boardTimings`), read at every board call and before each wait of the reaper's beat. See [The core](core.md#the-task-board).

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `board.leaseTtlMinutes` | number | `30` | Minutes a claim holds a task when the claim or the heartbeat names no lease of its own | `src/board/board.ts` |
| `board.autoTriage.role` | string | `"dev"` | The role `task.add` with `auto` fills in when the caller left it out | `src/board/board.ts` |
| `board.autoTriage.budget` | number | `4` | The budget in USD `task.add` with `auto` fills in when the caller left it out | `src/board/board.ts` |
| `board.autoTriage.steps` | number | `80` | The step cap `task.add` with `auto` fills in when the caller left it out | `src/board/board.ts` |
| `board.autoTriage.estimate` | number | `30` | The estimate in minutes `task.add` with `auto` fills in when the caller left it out | `src/board/board.ts` |
| `board.projects` | map | `{}` | Per project: `autoTriage` overrides the board-wide one field by field, and `ci: false` marks a project without CI, whose tasks a reviewer merges on recorded passing tests | `src/board/board.ts` |
| `board.reapSeconds` | number | `60` | Seconds between two beats of the reaper, which returns each task whose lease expired to `approved` (`1` to `3600`) | `src/board/board.ts` |
| `board.briefWaitMs` | number | `1800000` | Milliseconds `task.next` holds back a task whose answer no reviewer has acted on yet (`0` to 7 days) | `src/board/board.ts` |

## `wakes`

Settings for the wake engine every wake kind shares: the scheduler's tick, the mode, the caps, the tool loop and the retries of an inner turn, and the limits of each wake kind under `wakes.kinds`. The heartbeat and the selfimprovement wake keep their own limits in their sections. See [Inner life](inner-life.md).

| Key | Type | Default | What it does | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wakes.mode` | string | `"shadow"` | `shadow`: reads run, other calls are recorded but never executed. `live`: calls run on her grants | `src/behavior/inner.ts` |
| `wakes.tickSeconds` | number | `60` | How often the scheduler looks at what is due | `src/core.ts` |
| `wakes.review.historyDays` | number | `14` | Days of her own lines that decide when the review happens | `src/behavior/inner/settings.ts` |
| `wakes.caps.perChain` | number | `3` | Inner turns of one chain per local day | `src/behavior/inner.ts` |
| `wakes.loop.maxSteps` | number | `4` | Tool loop bounds of an inner turn | `src/turn/settings.ts` |
| `wakes.loop.timeBudgetMs` | number | `180000` | Time budget of an inner turn's calls | `src/memory/db/service.ts` |
| `wakes.loop.maxCallsPerStep` | number | `4` | Calls per answer of an inner turn | `src/turn/settings.ts` |
| `wakes.loop.callTimeoutMs` | number | `60000` | Max time per call of an inner turn | `src/turn/tool-round.ts` |
| `wakes.retry.delaysMinutes` | array | `[1, 5, 15, 60]` | Retry delays after a provider failure (minutes) | `src/behavior/inner/settings.ts` |
| `wakes.retry.maxHours` | number | `6` | Hours before retries stop | `src/behavior/inner/settings.ts` |
| `wakes.factsKeepDays` | number | `7` | Days an untold fact stays | `src/behavior/inner/settings.ts` |
| `wakes.kinds.*.tools` | string, array | `"*"` | The tools a wake of the kind may call: `"*"` (when unset) for every granted tool or a list of tool names | `src/tools/access.ts` |
| `wakes.kinds.*.maxActs` | number, null | `null` | The most actions a wake of the kind may take; unset or null: no cap | `src/tools/access.ts` |
| `wakes.kinds.*.maxTasks` | number, null | `null` | The most errands a wake of the kind may start; unset or null: no cap | `src/tools/access.ts` |
| `wakes.kinds.*.inputTokens` | number, null | `null` | The input token budget of a wake of the kind; unset or null: the loop budget | `src/tools/access.ts` |
